questions.title: Merge Sort a Vector
questions.description:
Implement merge sort: recursively split the range at its midpoint, sort both halves, then merge them. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> merge_sort(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the vector sorted ascending. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Quicksort a Vector
questions.description:
Implement quicksort: partition the range around a pivot (Lomuto scheme with the last element as pivot), then recurse into the two sides. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> quick_sort(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the vector sorted ascending. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Lomuto Partition Index
questions.description:
Run ONE Lomuto partition pass on the whole vector. The pivot is the LAST element. Scan j from 0 to n-2: whenever v[j] <= pivot, extend the "small" region and swap v[j] into it. Finally swap the pivot into position i+1 and return that index. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int lomuto_partition(std::vector<int> &v)

The vector is partitioned in place; the harness prints the pivot index, then the partitioned vector on the next line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the final pivot index. Line 2: the partitioned vector.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Halves
questions.description:
A vector's first floor(n/2) elements are sorted ascending and its remaining tail is sorted ascending as well. Perform the merge step of merge sort on the two halves in one linear sweep. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> merge_halves(const std::vector<int> &v)

It must return the fully sorted merge. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (each half sorted ascending).

Output Format:
One line with the merged, fully sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Merge Sort Recursion Depth
questions.description:
Merge sort halves the range until pieces hold one element, so its recursion depth is the smallest d with 2^d >= n. Compute it with a loop that doubles a size counter — no log, no pow. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long merge_depth(long long n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the smallest d such that 2^d >= n (0 for n = 1).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: Check the Partition Property
questions.description:
After a partition pass around index p, every element before p must be <= v[p] and every element after p must be >= v[p]. Write the validator. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool is_partitioned(const std::vector<int> &v, int p)

The harness prints 1 when the property holds, 0 otherwise.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: p (0 <= p < n).

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 0 <= p < n, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.description:

questions.title: Pick the Sorter for the Device
questions.description:
An embedded device reserves one auxiliary slot per element BEFORE sorting: if n <= budget it runs merge sort (which needs that buffer), otherwise it falls back to quicksort. Given n and the buffer budget, report which sorter the device runs. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string pick_sort(long long n, long long budget)

It must return "MergeSort" when n <= budget, else "QuickSort".

Input Format:
One line with n and budget.

Output Format:
One line with MergeSort or QuickSort.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000000000000, 0 <= budget <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: Merge Steps in Merge Sort
questions.description:
Instrument merge sort to count its merge steps. Use EXACTLY this scheme: recurse on [lo, mid) and [mid, hi) with mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 and base case when the range has 0 or 1 elements; the merge writes elements into a temporary array — count ONE step for EVERY element written into that temporary (taking from the left half on ties, then draining the remainders). The copy back into the vector does NOT count. Example: [3, 1, 2] takes 5 merge steps. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void merge_sort_count(std::vector<int> &v, long long &steps)

The harness prints the sorted vector, then the step count on the next line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sorted vector. Line 2: the total merge steps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Kth Smallest Ticket Number
questions.description:
A support queue holds ticket numbers with duplicates; the kth smallest counts duplicates (k is 1-based). Find it WITHOUT calling a library sort — quickselect with a Lomuto partition (last element as pivot) is the intended tool. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int kth_smallest(std::vector<int> v, int k)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated ticket numbers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the kth smallest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= k <= n, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Three-Way Partition of Mail
questions.description:
A mail sorter groups letters around a priority value, keeping each group in its ORIGINAL relative order (a stable three-way partition): first everything < pivot, then everything == pivot, then everything > pivot. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void three_way_partition(std::vector<int> &v, int pivot)

The harness prints the reordered vector space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: pivot.

Output Format:
One line with the partitioned vector.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values, pivot <= 1000000

questions.title: Merge Comparisons in Merge Sort
questions.description:
Instrument merge sort to count element COMPARISONS. Use EXACTLY the standard scheme: recurse on [lo, mid) and [mid, hi) with mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, base case 0 or 1 elements. During a merge, each evaluation of "left element <= right element" is ONE comparison; draining a remainder half and copying back compare nothing. Example: [2, 1] costs 1 comparison, [3, 1, 2] costs 3. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void merge_sort_comp(std::vector<int> &v, long long &comparisons)

The harness prints the sorted vector, then the comparison count on the next line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sorted vector. Line 2: the total comparisons.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Hoare Partition Point
questions.description:
Run ONE Hoare partition pass on the whole vector, exactly as defined: capture the pivot as the FIRST element once; then repeat — advance i while v[i] < pivot, retreat j while v[j] > pivot; if i >= j return j, otherwise swap v[i] and v[j] and continue. Return the split point j. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int hoare_partition(std::vector<int> &v)

The harness prints j, then the partitioned vector on the next line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the returned index j. Line 2: the partitioned vector.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Bottom-Up Merge Sort
questions.description:
A stack-limited device needs merge sort WITHOUT recursion. Implement it bottom-up: merge runs of width 1, then 2, then 4, ... doubling the width each round until one run covers the array (each round merges consecutive run pairs [i, i+width) and [i+width, i+2*width), clamped to n). Calling a sort routine is banned; no recursion allowed. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> bottom_up_merge(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the vector sorted ascending. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Counting Inversions Fast
questions.description:
An inversion is a pair of positions i < j with v[i] > v[j] — a direct measure of how unsorted the data is. Count them in O(n log n) by augmenting merge sort: when the merge takes an element from the RIGHT half while the left half still has i elements pending, those i elements all form inversions with it. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long inversion_count(std::vector<int> v)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the number of inversions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Comparison Duel: Merge vs Quick
questions.description:
Two sorting modules are benchmarked on the same data. Report how many element comparisons each performs, under these EXACT rules. Merge sort: recurse on [lo, mid) and [mid, hi) with mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, base case 0 or 1 elements; during a merge each evaluation of "left <= right" is one comparison; draining remainders and copying back compare nothing. Quicksort: on range [lo, hi] (inclusive) with pivot v[hi], the Lomuto scan compares each of the hi - lo elements v[lo..hi-1] against the pivot exactly once (moves happen when v[j] <= pivot); after the split recurse on [lo, p-1] and [p+1, hi]; ranges of length <= 1 compare nothing. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void compare_counts(std::vector<int> v, long long &mergeComp, long long &quickComp)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with mergeComp, then quickComp, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Stable Standings via Merge Sort
questions.description:
A contest must rank players by score ascending, STABLY: equal scores keep arrival order. Achieve it with merge sort that takes from the LEFT half on ties (that is exactly what makes merge sort stable). You receive keys (line 2) and arrival ids (line 3, aligned by position); return the ids in the stable order. std::sort and std::stable_sort are banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> merge_sort_ids(const std::vector<int> &keys, const std::vector<int> &ids)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated keys. Line 3: n distinct space-separated ids.

Output Format:
One line with the ids in stable key order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= keys <= 1000000, ids distinct

questions.title: Quicksort Pivot Flight Recorder
questions.description:
A teaching tool records which pivot positions quicksort chooses. Run quicksort with this EXACT scheme: on range [lo, hi] (inclusive) with at least 2 elements, run a Lomuto partition with pivot v[hi] (move while v[j] <= pivot), record the returned pivot index p, then recurse into [lo, p-1] FIRST and [p+1, hi] after. Return the sorted vector and the recorded pivot indices in order. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void quicksort_trace(std::vector<int> &v, std::vector<int> &pivots)

The harness prints the sorted vector, then the recorded pivot indices space-separated on the next line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sorted vector. Line 2: the recorded pivot indices.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000
